title: Per-region affinity convergence triggered queue oscillation; postmortem and follow-up playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Short summary: On 2025-10-04 a surge originating from a downstream partner caused uneven regional fanout. Region-eu-west developed persistent queue pressure leading to circuit breakers triggering and a multi-region oscillation as traffic failed over to other regions. This produced an SLO miss for 99p tail latency and increased token cost due to repeated model warmups.
timeline: 2025-10-04T09:23Z - Partner sent a large burst of evaluation traffic; 09:26Z - region-eu-west ingress queue grew past 75% capacity; 09:29Z - regional CB (hysteresis=15s) tripped and failed over to secondary regions; 09:31Z - secondary regions saw elevated concurrency; 09:33Z - warm-kv-cache cold miss observed as many requests routed to fresh replicas; 09:35Z - regional CBs started oscillating as failback thresholds were met; 09:50Z - on-call throttled partner traffic at control plane; 10:00Z - manual sticky-routing enabled for in-flight tokens; 12:30Z - load normalized; 14:00Z - incident declared resolved.
detection: Alerts: 99p latency SLO alert fired for API route /v1/generate (Alert ID: SLO-API-9904). Dashboards showed a 4x increase in token-per-request cost for the affected window. Observability traces indicated repeated cold KV cache initializations and increased kernel context switches on the serving hosts.
mitigation: Immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily increased circuit-breaker hysteresis from 15s to 60s for region-eu-west to prevent flip-flopping; 2) Enabled sticky affinity for active connections for 10 minutes to drain queues; 3) Applied emergency kv-cache prewarm for popular prefixes; 4) Configured partner-side rate-limiter to cap burst to 100 req/s per tenant. These reduced oscillation and tail latency within 30 minutes.
root_cause: Three factors combined: (A) a partner-generated burst with highly correlated prompts causing concentrated resource pressure in eu-west; (B) circuit-breaker hysteresis tuned aggressively for fast recovery (15s) which allowed flip-flop between regions under transient spikes; (C) implicit assumption in routing that replicas had 'warm' KV cache leading to frequent model warmups when traffic migrated. Secondary contributors: control-plane admitted bursts without tenant-level burst caps; autoscaler did not scale quickly because scale-up thresholds were tuned to CPU rather than queue depth.
impact: - SLO miss: 99p tail latency exceeded target for ~27 minutes for affected route; - Customer-visible errors: ~0.7% 5xx increase during peak; - Cost: ~2.4x token-compute cost for the incident window due to warmups; - Internal ops time: ~3.5 engineer-hours to mitigate and stabilize.
postmortem_notes: We confirmed no data loss. External partner cooperated and implemented immediate burst caps. No security issues identified. This incident surfaced brittle interactions between routing, CB hysteresis, and cache-warmup assumptions.
action_items: 1) ENG-862431: Apply region-aware circuit hysteresis defaults (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-11-07) - change default hysteresis to 45s for regions with <2x spare capacity and add per-region override; 2) ENG-862432: Implement queue-depth based autoscaling trigger (owner: Marco Li, due: 2025-11-14) - autoscaler to consider queue depth and KV-cache warmup rate; 3) ENG-862433: Add immutable warm-cache handoff + prewarm API (owner: Sofia Martin, due: 2025-10-24) - allow control plane to request prewarm for specific model prefixes before failover; 4) Policy: enforce tenant-level burst caps for public partners and expose burst metrics to partners (owner: GrowthOps, due: 2025-10-31); 5) Observability: create an SLO composite chart combining CB flip counts, KV cold-miss rate, and 99p latency (owner: Observability team, due: 2025-10-21).
owners_and_status: ENG-862431 (Priya Shah) - In Progress; ENG-862432 (Marco Li) - Planned; ENG-862433 (Sofia Martin) - In Progress; Partner coordination (GrowthOps) - Done; Observability dashboard - In Progress.
verification_plan: - Load test (synthetic burst) against canary cluster to reproduce flip behavior and verify hysteresis defangs oscillation; - Run prewarm+failover sequence and measure KV cold-miss rate <5%; - Validate autoscaler scales within target window under queued load; - Re-run partner-sourced traffic with burst cap and confirm no SLO regressions.
retrospective_notes: Key learnings: (1) hysteresis tuned for availability can amplify oscillations if cache-warmup cost is high; (2) multi-region routing requires explicit prewarm or sticky tokens during rapid rebalances; (3) SLO alerts should correlate CB flip counters as an early signal. Next steps: include these correlations in the alerting rulebook and document region isolation runbook.
communication: Incident report published to #oncall and #prod-postmortems channels. Customer-facing summary sent to impacted partners with recommended client-side rate-limits. Exec briefing completed 2025-10-06.
notes: Follow-up checklist created; weekly review scheduled in Cycle 42 to confirm mitigations are complete.
